metais reads, validates and renders METAIS packages, and helps author them.

A package (a .metais file) is a zip archive that is read only with metais, in
place: do not unzip it, and do not open it with any other zip tool or library,
not even to read one file in memory. Start with 'metais inspect <package>',
which shows what the package needs and the commands to run next. Then 'metais
read <package> <entry>' prints one of its entries, 'metais ls <package>' lists
them and 'metais grep <package> <pattern>' searches them.

Usage:
  metais <command> [operands] [flags]

Golden paths:
  Consuming a package: inspect → read → schema → validate → render; preview from
  generated data with render --sample, or start from data generated by sample
  Authoring a package: init → edit (preview with render --sample) → check → test
  → pack

Commands:
  Reading a package:
    inspect   Print what a supplier reads first: the package's identity, its
              guide, its inputs, outputs, references and examples, and the
              commands to run next.
    ls        List the entries under a path of a package.
    read      Print an entry of a package, or a range of its lines.
    outline   List the headings of a Markdown entry, each with the lines of its
              section.
    grep      Search a package's entries for a regular expression, with context.
    schema    Print the package's combined input schema, or one input's schema,
              or list their fields.
    extract   Write the entries the globs select to a directory.
  Supplying and rendering:
    validate  Validate inputs against a package, and report every finding at
              once.
    render    Render the package's outputs from the inputs supplied, into a
              directory or to standard output.
    sample    Generate sample data from the inputs' schemas, and keep it as a
              data directory or an example.
  Authoring:
    init      Write a new package's source directory: a greeting to learn from,
              or with --minimal one input and one template to replace.
    check     Check a package without data, and report every finding of every
              step at once, or only the refusal of a package that cannot be
              read.
    test      Render every example of a package and compare it with the outputs
              it should produce.
    pack      Check and test a source directory, then write it as one package
              file.
    unpack    Write a packed package's source directory, to edit it.
  The tool:
    version   Print the tool's version and the specification versions it
              implements.
    limits    List every resource limit, with its default, unit and class.
    skill     Write metais's agent skill, which teaches a coding agent the
              golden paths, where the agent's harness reads skills.
    help      Print the overview, a command's help, or a topic.

Global flags:
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.
  --version
      Run metais version.

Topics (metais help <topic>):
  inputs      Supplying a package's inputs, and which source wins.
  templates   Writing templates: the environment, every filter, and escaping.
  manifest    Every field of metais.yaml, inputs and outputs included.
  globs       The patterns that select a package's entries.
  json        The JSON document every command prints with --json.
  exit-codes  What each exit status means.
  refusals    Every code a command may refuse with: metais help refusals
              <command>.

Exit codes:
  0  Success, warnings included; help, version and limits.
  1  An error in content: invalid inputs, a failing check or test, an output
     refused by its schema or its path, a package's own defect under an
     authoring command, or a warning under --fail-on warning.
  2  A defect in metais itself (internal.error, or internal.memory when it stops
     a command holding more memory than it allows itself), or the Go runtime's
     status after a crash.
  3  The command line is wrong: an unknown command or flag, a missing or extra
     operand, a malformed or repeated flag, or no command at all.
  4  The package is refused: not found, unreadable, out of specification, a
     digest mismatch, an unsupported specification version or a package limit;
     or a package's own defect under a consuming command.
  5  The destination is refused: not empty without --overwrite, a link or
     special file in the way, or a failed write.

Run 'metais help <command>' or 'metais <command> --help' for a command's
operands, flags, refusals and examples.
